organizations.name: Trinity Episcopal Cathedral
organizations.description: Free bag lunches, coffee, and dog/cat food. No ID required, everyone welcome. Historic cathedral overlooking the Truckee River in downtown Reno.

organizations.name: St. Vincent Dining Room
organizations.description: Free hot lunch served daily, serving over 1,400 people. Everyone welcome, 7 days a week.

organizations.name: Family Soup at Believe Plaza
organizations.description: Free dinner served every Tuesday evening. Community meal for anyone in need. Run by volunteers and community members.

contacts.value: Believe Plaza, 1 N Sierra St, Reno, NV 89501

organizations.name: Mutual Aid Mondays at Our Center
organizations.description: Weekly mutual aid gathering every Monday at 5PM. A collaborative space to strengthen community through sharing knowledge, resources, and wisdom. All ages and identities welcome.

organizations.name: Food Bank of Northern Nevada
organizations.description: Food distribution, mobile pantries, and emergency food assistance serving 160,000+ people monthly across 13 Nevada counties and 10 California counties. Note: Food distributions are NOT held at the warehouse - use their Food Finder tool.

organizations.name: Hampton House Garden
organizations.description: Black-led community garden with 24/7 open-access food pantry and refrigerator. Multi-generational space hosting community garden, food recovery compost, harm reduction supplies, and organizing venue. No requirements to receive food.

organizations.name: Catholic Charities of Northern Nevada
organizations.description: Comprehensive resource hub including food assistance, emergency aid, and social services. St. Vincent's programs serve thousands annually.

organizations.name: Good Neighbors Warming Centers
organizations.description: Overnight warming centers rotating between churches (Trinity Episcopal, First United Methodist, Good Shepherd Lutheran, St. Thomas Aquinas). Safe overnight shelter with meals and warmth through March 31. Coordinated by Hampton House Garden, RISE, and community partners.

contacts.value: 9:00 PM - 6:00 AM, 7 days/week during cold season

organizations.eligibility: Women, families, single dads with children. Single men directed to CARES Campus.

organizations.name: Volunteers of America Nevada CARES Campus
organizations.description: Emergency shelter for up to 600 adults experiencing homelessness. Clients can bring partners, pets, and possessions. Provides support services, case management, housing navigation, mental health counseling, and meals.

organizations.name: CrossRoads Program (Washoe County HSA)
organizations.description: Peer-led, alcohol and drug-free structured housing program with integrated wrap-around supportive services. Offers intensive case management, life skills development, workforce readiness programming, healthcare connections, and continuing care support for alumni.
organizations.eligibility: Men, women, women with children, and families seeking structured, supportive, alcohol and drug-free living

organizations.name: Battle Born Housing Plus (Catholic Charities)
organizations.description: Recovery residence program providing housing and supportive services for low-income men recovering from substance use disorder. 58 residential units including studio apartments and congregate living. Services include case management, substance abuse counseling, behavioral health support, employment opportunities, and peer support. First in Nevada to earn NARR certification.
organizations.eligibility: Low-income men recovering from substance use disorder

organizations.name: Hope Springs (Northern Nevada HOPES)
organizations.description: Northern Nevada's first bridge housing community. Different from a shelter - provides privacy, safety, autonomy with shared resources. Through safe housing, behavioral health, and wrap-around services, residents build a path toward independent living. Close to 50 residents have moved into permanent housing.

organizations.name: Safe Camp
organizations.description: Transitional housing program at Governors Bowl Park providing structured support for individuals moving toward permanent housing.

contacts.value: Governors Bowl Park, Line Dr, Reno, NV 89512

organizations.name: Eddy House
organizations.description: Youth shelter and services for young adults ages 12-24 experiencing homelessness or housing instability. Includes TLC 360 apartments for transitional housing.

organizations.name: Our Place / RISE
organizations.description: Low-barrier, person-first emergency shelter and resource center in partnership with Washoe County HSA. Provides services, referrals, and support for individuals experiencing homelessness. A place where guests feel welcomed and wanted.

organizations.name: Nevada Youth Empowerment Project (NYEP)
organizations.description: Housing and support services for youth ages 16-24 aging out of foster care or experiencing homelessness. Provides apartments and life skills training.

organizations.name: Karma Box Project
organizations.description: Nonprofit providing hope and opportunity for people experiencing homelessness. Helps clients obtain permanent housing, increase income, improve health, and regain stability and self-sufficiency through projects, programming, and community engagement. Founded by Grant Denton in 2018.

contacts.value: 100 N Arlington Ave Suite 250, Reno, NV 89501

organizations.name: P.U.F. House (WellCare Foundation)
organizations.description: Transitional housing and crisis stabilization services. Part of WellCare Foundation programs providing recovery and housing support.

organizations.name: The Life Change Center
organizations.description: Residential and outpatient treatment programs for substance use disorders. Multiple locations in Reno, Sparks, and Carson City.

organizations.name: Reno Housing Authority
organizations.description: Section 8 vouchers, public housing, and rental assistance programs for low-income residents.

organizations.name: Safe Embrace
organizations.description: Emergency shelter and support services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. 24-hour crisis line available.

organizations.description: Legal assistance for tenants facing eviction, housing discrimination, and landlord-tenant disputes.

organizations.description: Community health center providing medical, dental, behavioral health, and HIV/AIDS services regardless of ability to pay.

organizations.name: Northern Nevada HOPES - Sexual Health
organizations.description: Free and confidential STI/HIV testing, PrEP, and sexual health services.

organizations.name: Community Health Alliance

organizations.name: Change Point
organizations.description: Harm reduction services including syringe exchange, HIV/Hepatitis testing, and naloxone distribution.

organizations.name: Washoe County Community Health Services
organizations.description: Public health services including immunizations, TB testing, STI testing, and family planning. Sliding fee scale available.

organizations.name: Reno-Sparks Tribal Health Center
organizations.description: Comprehensive health services for Native American community members including medical, dental, pharmacy, and behavioral health.

organizations.description: Health and social services for urban Native Americans including medical care, behavioral health, and community programs. Services available to all populations regardless of insurance, with discounted rates based on income.
organizations.eligibility: Native American individuals and families (all populations welcome)

organizations.name: VA Homeless Veteran Care
organizations.description: Health care, housing assistance, and support services for veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Provides immediate food and shelter, transitional and permanent housing, job training, and mental health treatment.

organizations.name: WellCare Health Services
organizations.description: Comprehensive behavioral health services including crisis stabilization, medical detox, and outpatient treatment.

organizations.description: Nevada Medicaid managed care plan with medical, behavioral health, pharmacy, and transportation benefits.

organizations.name: SilverSummit Healthplan
organizations.description: Nevada Medicaid managed care plan providing comprehensive health coverage and member support services.

organizations.name: DWSS Sparks Office
organizations.description: Sparks district office for Nevada welfare services including SNAP, TANF, and Medicaid applications.

organizations.description: Free, confidential 24/7 resource hotline connecting Nevadans to essential services including food, housing, healthcare, mental health, and support for children, families, seniors, and people with disabilities. Translation services in 150+ languages.

organizations.description: National crisis line for anyone experiencing suicidal thoughts, mental health crisis, or emotional distress. Free, confidential support 24/7. If calling 911, ask for a Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Officer.

organizations.name: NAMI Northern Nevada
organizations.description: Free mental health support, education, and advocacy. Offers support groups, educational programs, and 24-hour emergency resources including mobile outreach safety team and crisis support hotline. Helps residents access quality housing, employment, healthcare, and education.

organizations.name: DCFS Mobile Crisis Response Team
organizations.description: Mobile crisis response and stabilization services for youth under 18. Provides community-based mental health therapy, medication management, early childhood day treatment, and wraparound care coordination.

organizations.name: Reno Behavioral Healthcare Hospital
organizations.description: Free and confidential mental health assessments available 24/7 to help determine the best treatment plan. Provides inpatient and outpatient mental health services.

organizations.name: Washoe County Senior Services
organizations.description: Comprehensive services for adults 60+ including nutritious meals, in-home assistance, emotional health programs, residential care, and financial management support. Programs include homemaker services, case management, representative payee, and group homes.

organizations.name: Washoe Senior Ride (Taxi Bucks)
organizations.description: Subsidized taxi program for seniors. Provides transportation assistance for medical appointments, shopping, and other essential trips.

organizations.name: Food Bank Senior Nutrition Program
organizations.description: Monthly food boxes for seniors 60+ through the USDA Commodity Supplemental Food Program. Provides nutritious food to supplement diets of low-income elderly.

organizations.name: Nevadaworks / EmployNV Career Hub
organizations.description: One-stop shop for free career services including job search assistance, resume help, skills training, and career counseling. Good Jobs Northern Nevada program provides free training in healthcare, IT, manufacturing, and logistics with support services like childcare and transportation.

contacts.value: 4001 S Virginia St, Ste H, Reno, NV 89502

organizations.description: Free employment services for job seekers of all backgrounds. Provides skill-building, training, and removes barriers to employment. Connects job seekers with opportunities in aerospace, construction, healthcare, IT, manufacturing, mining, and tourism.

organizations.name: Nevada DETR (Employment, Training & Rehabilitation)
organizations.description: State workforce agency providing job placement, training, unemployment insurance, services for people with disabilities, and labor market data. Many services provided through EmployNV Career Hubs.

organizations.name: The Children's Cabinet
organizations.description: Child care subsidy assistance for income-eligible families so they can work, receive job training, or finish education. Subsidies cover up to 100% of child care costs with copays of $0, $90, or $150/month based on income. Priority for children with special needs, homeless children, and very low-income families.
organizations.eligibility: Income-based (at or below 41% State Median Income)

organizations.name: RTC Washoe Reduced Fare Program
organizations.description: Reduced bus fare of $0.75 (vs $2.00 regular) for seniors 60+, individuals with disabilities or Medicare cards, and U.S. Veterans. Buy passes via Token Transit app.

organizations.name: Access to Healthcare Network - Medical Transportation
organizations.description: FREE non-emergency medical transportation for seniors, disabled individuals, and low-income residents in Reno and Greater Washoe County. Senior Ambassador Program provides free rides for eligible Medicare patients.

organizations.name: MTM Health - Medicaid Transportation
organizations.description: Free non-emergency transportation for Nevada Medicaid members to covered appointments. Offers reloadable debit card for public transit day passes. Must schedule rides in advance.

organizations.name: DAV Vans for Veterans
organizations.description: Free van rides to and from VA Sierra Nevada Healthcare System for veterans who don't have other transportation options. Ambulatory passengers only (able to move without driver assistance).

organizations.name: Catholic Charities Immigration Legal Services
organizations.description: Mother Cabrini Immigration Legal Services providing high quality, low-cost or pro bono immigration legal services since 2006. Helps foreign-born individuals and families obtain or extend lawful immigration status or citizenship.

organizations.name: PLAN Citizenship & Immigration Program
organizations.description: DOJ-recognized and accredited immigration services. Assists with adjustment of status, DACA, family petitions, Temporary Protected Status (TPS), and EOIR proceedings.

organizations.name: Nevada Disability Advocacy & Law Center (NDALC)
organizations.description: Nevada's federally-mandated protection and advocacy system for human, legal, and service rights for individuals with disabilities. Provides information, referral, technical assistance, training, legal and non-legal advocacy, and outreach.

contacts.value: 2820 W Charleston Blvd #11, Las Vegas, NV 89102

organizations.name: Nevada Aging & Disability Services (ADSD)
organizations.description: State agency ensuring older adults and individuals with disabilities have access to essential programs and resources. Programs include Autism Treatment Assistance, Office of Community Living, and independent living support.

contacts.value: 3416 Goni Rd D-132, Carson City, NV 89706

organizations.name: Nevada Assistive Technology Resource Center
organizations.description: Part of Nevada Center for Excellence in Disabilities at UNR. Offers device loans, demonstrations, and training to help individuals with disabilities explore and use assistive technology effectively.

organizations.name: Our Center (LGBTQ+ Community Center)
organizations.description: Safe, empowering, and supportive center for the LGBTQ+ community. Offers support groups for youth and adult trans members, senior community groups, prevention-focused initiatives, education, and job information.

organizations.name: Northern Nevada Pride
organizations.description: LGBTQ+ advocacy, community events, and Pride celebrations. Supports the activities of Our Center. Promotes rights and wellbeing of the LGBTQ+ community through public awareness and events.

organizations.name: HOPES LGBTQ & Gender Healthcare
organizations.description: The Barry Frank Family Gender and Sexual Healthcare Clinic provides culturally competent, judgment-free health care including gender affirming resources, case management, and financial support for individuals transitioning.

organizations.name: Catholic Charities Reentry Programs
organizations.description: Reentry and recovery programs for formerly incarcerated individuals including Battle Born Housing Plus and St. Marguerite Support Services. Designed to reduce recidivism, promote recovery, provide basic needs, and support long-term reintegration.

organizations.name: Life Changes, Inc.
organizations.description: Statewide reentry services for individuals released from Nevada Department of Corrections. Provides transportation from parole office, intake assistance, help purchasing necessities like phones, and ongoing support.

organizations.name: NV Energy Assistance Programs
organizations.description: Utility assistance programs for customers struggling to pay electric and gas bills. Includes payment plans, budget billing, and connections to LIHEAP and other assistance programs.
